Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) enquired. When the people confirmed that he did, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) took an oath saying, "It is to Allaah that I vow never to speak to Ibn Zubayr ever again!"
When the separation became too long for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA), he sent people to intercede on his behalf, but Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "By Allaah! I shall never accept the intercession of anyone on his behalf and I shall never break my vow." When it became too much for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) to bear, he spoke to Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhramah (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Aswad bin Abd Yaghooth (RA) who both belonged to the Banu Zuhrah tribe. He pleaded with them saying, "I beseech you in the name of Allaah to get me into the house of Aa'isha (RA) because it is not permissible for her to take a vow to severe ties with me.
Consequently, Hadhrat Miswar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) hid Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) in their shawls and sought permission to enter from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) saying:

"May we come in." When Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) gave them permission to enter, they asked, "Can we all come in?" "Of course," replied Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) not knowing that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) was with them, "you may all come in." As soon as they entered, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) rushed behind the veil and embracing Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), he started weeping and pleading with her in the name of Allaah.
Hadhrat Miswar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) also pleaded with her in the name of Allaah that she should speak to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) and accept his apology. They also said to her, "As you know, Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade severing of ties and that it is not permissible for a Muslim to severe ties with a Muslim brother for more than three days." When they took pains to remind her and were persistent, she started to weep as she addressed the two men saying, "I have taken and oath and an oath is a serious matter."
They however continued convincing her until she started speaking to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA). As expiation for her broken vow, she then freed forty slaves and whenever she thought about the vow, she wept so much that her tears would wet her scarf.[^1]

Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ and (her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) loved Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) the most and he always treated her most kindly. Whenever she received anything, she would never keep it with her and always gave it away in charity. Concerning this, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) once remarked, "Her hands ought to be held back." (When she heard about this remark) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "Should my hands be held back?! It is to Allaah that I vow never to speak to him (Ibn Zubayr) ever again!" Even though men of the Quraysh and particularly the maternal uncles of Rasulullaah ﷺ
